thread:
customer_ops_sam: Hey team — Acme (dedicated pool dp-782) is seeing a sudden spike of 429s starting ~04:12 UTC after we migrated them to the new enterprise plan. Customer says traffic pattern didn't change. Can we triage?

support_engineer_jamie: I'm on it. Can you paste a sample request id and the tenant quota config if you have it?

customer_ops_sam: Request id: req_0b9f3a. Attaching the tenant quota snippet from the migration job:```json
{"tenant_id":"acme","pool_id":"dp-782","quota": {"rate_limit": {"units": 100, "granularity": "minute"}, "burst": 200}}
```

infra_oncall_marta: Pulling metrics for dp-782 now. I see a sharp drop in allowed throughput at 04:12 and queueing on the pool. CPU/GPU utilization is normal; autoscaler didn't spin up new nodes — it looks like requests are being rejected before they hit the dispatcher.

eng_runtime_lee: That quota JSON stands out — we expect plan migrations to express rate_limit in "hour" for enterprise plans (our migration script should convert but probably didn't). If it's interpreted as per-minute, effective capacity is 60x lower than intended.

support_engineer_jamie: Quick math: intended 100 units/hour -> ~1.67 units/min. The config set 100/min -> 6000/hour. Wait that would increase not decrease... which direction did they expect?

customer_ops_sam: The target SLA says 6000 units/hour for this plan. The migration script was supposed to write units:6000, granularity:"hour". Looks like someone tried to make it human-friendly and wrote 100 with granularity minute (internal mistake). The customer's app is sending 200 req/min, which now hits the minute limit.

eng_runtime_lee: Ah — OK. So two mismatch issues: (1) migration wrote a smaller numeric value with a smaller granularity that makes it too tight; (2) our rate enforcement code treats the number literally for the given granularity. We need to get them unthrottled ASAP.

support_engineer_jamie: Short mitigation plan: (A) apply an immediate admin override to set quota to units:6000, granularity:"hour" for acme tenancy; (B) restart quota-sync worker for dp-782 to avoid stale cache; (C) roll a fix to the migration script to normalize units->hour.

billing_ops_noah: FYI — changing quotas affects billing metrics. I approve a short override for 30m while we patch. Will track in billing audit.

infra_oncall_marta: Running override command now:```bash
# admin CLI
redwood admin override set-quota --tenant acme --pool dp-782 --json '{"rate_limit": {"units": 6000, "granularity": "hour"}, "burst": 2400}'
```

deploy_bot: deploy-bot: override applied by marta — id override_20260317_001 — scope: tenant:acme pool:dp-782 TTL:30m

infra_oncall_marta: Restarting quota-sync worker for dp-782...```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/quota-sync-dp-782 -n redwood-serving```

support_engineer_jamie: After override + restart, I'm seeing 429 rate drop from ~1500/min to ~20/min within 30s. Queue depth dropping. Can we notify customer that we've applied a temporary override?

customer_ops_sam: Notified Acme. They confirmed errors stopped within a minute and are running regression tests. Thank you.

eng_runtime_lee: Next actions for PR: (1) patch migration tool to always write target numeric value in hours for enterprise/dedicated plans, with unit tests around boundary conversions; (2) add a guard in the quota API that rejects ambiguous granularity (e.g., prevent writing minute granularity for enterprise plans); (3) add an alert when quota changes >10x on migration. I'll take (1)+(2), file follow-up.

support_engineer_jamie: I'm creating a support postmortem thread and will include timeline + mitigation steps + customer comms. Please add logs/commands you ran.

billing_ops_noah: I'll reconcile billing for the override window and flag any anomalies.

customer_ops_sam: Acme says full traffic looks normal now. Keeping on standby for 1h to verify.

eng_runtime_lee: Patch PR opened: GH#redwood/infra-migrations PR 2345 — includes normalization + tests. ETA for merge + release: 2d (hotfix for migration pipeline).

support_engineer_jamie: Closing this Slack thread when postmortem is up. Thanks everyone. :tada:
